verses.text: So I decided not to make another painful visit to you.
If I cause you pain, who can make me glad except the person I hurt?
I wrote as I did so that, when I came, I wouldn't be saddened by the very people who should make me glad. I was confident that all of you would share in my joy.
I wrote to you with many tears and much pain in my heart—not to make you sad, but to show you how deeply I love you.
If anyone has caused sorrow, they haven't hurt me so much as they've hurt all of you, though I don't want to overstate it.
The punishment given by most of you to that person is enough.
Now you should forgive and comfort them instead. Otherwise, they may be overwhelmed by too much sorrow.
So I urge you to reaffirm your love for them.
I wrote to you for this reason too: I wanted to see whether you would stand the test and obey in everything.
If you forgive anyone, I forgive them too. And whatever I have forgiven—if there was anything to forgive—I have forgiven for your sake in Christ's presence,
so that Satan can't get the upper hand over us. We know how his schemes work.
When I came to Troas to share Christ's Good News, the Lord opened a door for me.
But I had no peace of mind because I couldn't find my brother Titus. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
Thanks be to God, who always leads us in Christ's victory parade and spreads the knowledge of him through us everywhere like a sweet fragrance.
We are the fragrance of Christ to God among those being saved and those who are perishing.
To some, we are a smell that leads from death to death; to others, a fragrance that leads from life to life. Who is up to this task?
We aren't like so many people who peddle God's word for profit. Instead, in Christ we speak sincerely, as people sent by God and standing in God's presence.
